findings.issue_text: P1: Transitional rule states removed — GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx now renders only promResponse rules; rules being created (ruler-only, RuleOperation.Creating) vanish from the list until the Prometheus API reflects them, and rules being deleted (prom-only, RuleOperation.Deleting) appear as fully actionable normal rows, letting users click Edit/Delete/Silence on rules that no longer exist

P1: AlertRuleMenu.tsx / RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx OR-combine ruler and folder/prom permission checks (canX = rulerX || grafanaX), which can grant enabled menu actions (Delete/Duplicate) whose handlers still require a ruler rule, causing enabled actions to fail on click when only a GrafanaPromRuleDTO is available

P2: GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx:41 dropped the paused-state fallback — old code used rule?.isPaused ?? is_paused, new code uses only rule?.isPaused, so if the Prometheus API omits/nulls isPaused, paused rules render as unpaused

P2: useAbilities.ts useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable returns { isEditable: false, isRemovable: false, loading: false } when !rule || !folderUID, treating 'no data yet' as definitively not editable; combined with MaybeSupported = loading ? NotSupported : AlwaysSupported this yields 'supported but denied' during load, causing UI flicker between actions hidden and visible, and invalid/missing folderUid silently removes all actions with no surfaced error

P3: RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx getEditableIdentifier calls logWarning('Unable to construct an editable rule identifier') during render on every render in the fallback path, spamming the analytics/warning channel at poll frequency for consumers passing only a non-Grafana prom rule

P3: GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx:31 dropped the returnTo parameter from rule view links — old code appended { returnTo } via createReturnTo(), so users navigating to a rule lose the return-to-list-with-filters-preserved behavior

Tests: RulesTable.test.tsx / GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx mocks hard-code the hook contract, so plural-hook tests pass even if per-action semantics change, and the deleted matchRules unit tests removed coverage for the ruler/prom propagation-race behavior

Permission checks weakened by OR-ing two independent ability sources: canX = (rulerSupported && rulerAllowed) || (grafanaSupported && grafanaAllowed) allows users denied on one surface but with incidental ability on the other to see and initiate actions (privilege inflation / client-side authz bypass)

Stale ruler-based ability path still consulted for Grafana rules: useRulerRuleAbilities treats undefined rule with defaults and derives rulesSourceName from groupIdentifier alone, allowing provisioned/plugin-provided rules to appear actionable and bypassing immutability guards

useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities marks all actions AlwaysSupported once loading completes, removing the 'feature unavailable' guard and making the grafana path's supported half always true so the effective gate is purely grafanaAllowed

N+1 folder/permission queries per rule row: useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities/useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable call useFolder(rule?.folderUid) and useCanSilenceInFolder per rule component, causing per-row fan-out of folder lookups, hook executions, and re-render work across ~80 rules per list page

Duplicate ability computation in AlertRuleMenu: both useRulerRuleAbilities and useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities always execute (10 ability evaluations per menu render), including useIsRuleEditable and useCanSilence(undefined) when rulerRule is undefined, doubling hook execution cost

Unstable actions array defeats memoization: AlertRuleMenu passes a new inline actions array literal each render, causing useMemo(() => actions.map(...)) in useRulerRuleAbilities/useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities to recompute every render and change returned Ability[] identity, breaking downstream memo/consumer equality
Ability checks OR'd together grant actions when only one path allows them, potentially allowing federated/provisioned rules to appear editable/deletable in the UI (privilege escalation risk in UI)
Grafana prom-rule path does not check isProvisioned for silence, and previous federated-rule immutability enforcement has silently been dropped

useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities asserts support before permissions load; if rule is defined but folderUid is missing, useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable permanently reports non-editable/non-removable with loading:false, so edit/delete buttons never appear

useGrafanaPromRuleAbility/useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities fetch folder permissions unconditionally per rule, causing N+1 folder metadata HTTP requests on the alert list page even for rules that end up skipped

Deleting/creating state indicators removed entirely from the Grafana list view: RuleOperation.Creating and RuleOperation.Deleting transitional states no longer rendered, so users lose feedback during ruler/prometheus propagation lag

RulesTable.test.tsx 'Grafana rules: should not render Edit button' test mocks useGrafanaPromRuleAbility (singular) which AlertRuleMenu never calls, making the mock dead code and the test not faithfully pinning the component-to-hook contract

Plural useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities default mock ignores the rule argument, so a non-Grafana promRule would still return [true,true], masking a real bug if the prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule() guard were removed

AlertRuleMenu silence support comes from two divergent sources (useCanSilence vs prom hook abilities) OR'd together, so type-detection mismatch between RulerGrafanaRuleDTO and GrafanaPromRuleDTO can show Silence menu items for invalid rules or hide previously working ones
useRulerRuleAbilities signature widened to accept undefined but the body may not guard against undefined, risking a runtime crash for callers passing undefined

P1: OR-combining abilities bypasses 'supported' gating — combining (rulerSupported && rulerAllowed) || (grafanaSupported && grafanaAllowed) can expose edit/delete/pause buttons when the ruler API is unavailable but user has folder permissions, causing operations to fail at execution time; ability checks should require both paths to agree on support

P1: Provisioning/immutability detection inconsistency — ruler path uses rule.grafana_alert.provenance while prom path uses isProvisionedPromRule/Boolean(provenance) from the prom DTO; if the APIs disagree on provenance, provisioned rules can be marked mutable and expose destructive Delete/Edit actions (data-loss vector)

P2: Refactor drops 'Creating'/'Deleting' rule state rendering and ruler-API reconciliation in GrafanaGroupLoader — ruler-only and prom-only transition rules no longer show indicators and the logWarning telemetry for mismatched rules was removed, making stuck/failing rule propagation invisible in the UI

P2: useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable/useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities conflate 'folder missing' with 'loading' — folder query errors leave MaybeSupported as AlwaysSupported so actions like Silence/Duplicate/Export still appear; no error-state handling for the folder query and rule-level check no longer factors isRulerAvailable into support
P2: returnTo dropped from rule list item links in GrafanaRuleListItem — new href omits returnTo from createReturnTo(), breaking back-navigation to the list view after viewing a rule

P3: useAllAlertRuleAbilities changed rulesSourceName derivation from getRulesSourceName(rule.namespace.rulesSource) to groupIdentifier origin — for federated/copied groups the permissions may be evaluated against the wrong data source

P3: Unused variable/redundant guard in GrafanaRuleListItem — promAlertingRule guard is redundant since rule is non-optional; flag to confirm prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule narrows the type correctly

RulesTable tests mock useRulerRuleAbilities and useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities, so the real hook implementations and the OR-combining logic in AlertRuleMenu.tsx and RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx are completely untested; a bug in the OR logic or skipToken guard would pass the suite

The OR-combination logic (canX = (rulerSupported && rulerAllowed) || (grafanaSupported && grafanaAllowed)) has zero behavioral tests, missing cases like ruler-supported-only, supported-but-not-allowed, undefined promRule with non-grafana ruler rule, and non-alerting grafana prom rules (e.g., recording rules should not show Pause)

GrafanaGroupLoader behavioral change removes Creating/Deleting states with old tests deleted, not replaced; no test covers a rule existing in prom whose ruler rule was just deleted, risking rules silently disappearing with no indicator or logWarning

Deleted matchRules unit tests leave no coverage for the new single-source rendering edge cases: a group with zero rules and a response where groups is empty (at(0) undefined) silently rendering an empty list

New hooks useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities / useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable lack direct tests for edge cases: missing folderUid, folder still loading (should suppress buttons, not flash-deny), undefined rule/skipToken path, provisioned rules with provenance, and non-alerting rules

GrafanaGroupLoader test hard-codes 'exactly 4 menu items' while granting Delete permission but never asserting Delete is present (implicitly asserting its absence); the brittle count also breaks if legitimate menu items are added

RulesTable cloud-rule tests assert only the mock (skipToken) rather than verified behavior; nothing verifies that a real Mimir/cloud rule correctly passes skipToken to useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities via the prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule type-guard

useAbilities.ts hardcodes isFederated = false with a TODO, dropping federated-rule immutability handling and showing Edit/Delete/Pause to users whose edits won't behave correctly (behavioral regression)

GrafanaGroupLoader no longer handles ruler/prom divergence: removed useGetGrafanaRulerGroupQuery, matchRules, and Creating/Deleting rendering, so rules silently vanish from the list during propagation and the logWarning mismatch observability is lost

hooks/useAbilities.ts duplicates ability-checking logic: useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable re-implements useIsRuleEditable (marked '// duplicate') and useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities copies ~60 lines of useAllRulerRuleAbilities, creating two parallel permission engines with drift risk

AlertRuleMenu.tsx has five copy-pasted 'OR two ability tuples' blocks (canPause, canDelete, canDuplicate, canSilence, canExport) with questionable OR semantics where the permissive path wins; should be centralized in a combineAbilities helper

useAllAlertRuleAbilities derives rules source from group origin instead of the rule's namespace rulesSource, potentially querying editability against the wrong datasource for mismatched combined rules
Custom skipToken Symbol in useAbilities.ts collides conceptually with RTK Query's skipToken sentinel, causing import and reader confusion; should be renamed (e.g. skipAbility) or reuse RTK concept

GrafanaRuleListItem drops is_paused fallback, provenance, and returnTo navigation context sourced from the ruler rule, so paused/provisioned indicators and back-navigation silently disappear if the Prometheus API doesn't return them
RulesTable.test.tsx duplicates mock implementations of up to 3-4 ability hooks per test and in beforeEach; should use a shared mockAbilities helper

RuleActionsButtons.V2 props type uses RequireAtLeastOne over two optional fields, which doesn't actually enforce at least one, and getEditableIdentifier/getIsProvisioned handle undefined/undefined at runtime; type should be a union like { rule } | { promRule }

useRulerRuleAbilities now accepts RulerRuleDTO | undefined and silently returns all-NotSupported abilities instead of a type error, moving the 'which rule am I checking' guard concern from types to call sites

P1: OR-union of ruler and grafana ability checks in AlertRuleMenu.tsx and RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx can grant actions the backend will reject, since the button can appear when only the other permission path said yes
P1: OR-union of ability checks masks permission bugs — if either hook is wrong, the other path's correct 'no' is silently overridden with no reconciliation or logging when the two disagree
P1: GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx rewrite removes ruler API fetch, so ruler-only rules (in 'Creating' state) vanish from the list until the prom rules endpoint catches up
P1: Removal of ruler API fetch means prom-only rules mid-deletion no longer show 'Deleting' state, appearing as live rules with full action buttons including Delete, inviting double-delete confusion
P1: Tests in GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx and RulesTable.test.tsx removed the matchRules unit tests and 'Creating'/'Deleting' state assertions, replacing them with happy-path-only tests

P1: RulesTable.test.tsx removed the useRulerRuleAbilities mock while the component ORs both hooks, so the 'should render edit button' test passes if either hook says yes, masking regressions in either hook individually (green-while-red test setup)

P2: isPluginProvidedRule is called with a GrafanaPromRuleDTO in useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities where it presumably always returns false, causing plugin-provided Grafana-managed rules to lose their immutability guard and become editable/deletable

P2: Type guards rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule) and prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) are invoked with possibly-undefined rule, which may throw at render for consumers passing skipToken/undefined instead of returning 'not supported'
P2: GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx drops returnTo from the href, losing 'back to list' navigation context when going from rule list to rule detail

P2: GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx removed the is_paused fallback (isPaused: rule?.isPaused only), so if the Prometheus rules API omits isPaused for Grafana-managed rules, paused rules will render as unpaused

P2: Provisioned detection switched from ruler rule provenance to prom rule provenance; if the prom endpoint doesn't surface provenance, provisioned rules will appear editable/deletable until UI writes fail

goldens.comment: The rendered GrafanaRuleListItem is missing the required key prop for React list items. This can cause rendering issues when the list order changes.

RuleActionsButtons is invoked with only promRule, but SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer inside RuleActionsButtons still depends on a Grafana Ruler rule being present, so for Grafana rules coming from list views the 'Silence notifications' menu entry (now driven by Grafana Prom abilities) will toggle showSilenceDrawer without ever rendering the drawer. This means clicking 'Silence notifications' for these rules has no visible effect, even when abilities indicate silencing is allowed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Transitional rule states removed — GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx now renders only promResponse rules; rules being created (ruler-only, RuleOperation.Creating) vanish from the list until the Prometheus API reflects them, and rules being deleted (prom-only, RuleOperation.Deleting) appear as fully actionable normal rows, letting users click Edit/Delete/Silence on rules that no longer exist

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the transitional-state handling in GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx: it no longer queries the ruler API, no longer calls matchRules(), and now renders only `promResponse.data.groups.at(0)?.rules.map(...)`, while the previous rendering of ruler-only rules with `operation={RuleOperation.Creating}` and prom-only rules via `RuleOperationListItem ... operation={RuleOperation.Deleting}` is deleted. This means any temporary mismatch between Ruler and Prometheus (create/delete propagation) would no longer be represented and prom-only rules would be rendered as normal actionable `GrafanaRuleListItem`s. However, whether such mismatches can still occur is not verifiable from the diff (the removed code even claimed strong consistency), so it’s a concrete edge-case/regression concern rather than a confirmed defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: AlertRuleMenu.tsx / RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx OR-combine ruler and folder/prom permission checks (canX = rulerX || grafanaX), which can grant enabled menu actions (Delete/Duplicate) whose handlers still require a ruler rule, causing enabled actions to fail on click when only a GrafanaPromRuleDTO is available

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows abilities in AlertRuleMenu are now computed as an OR between ruler-based abilities and new GrafanaPromRuleDTO-based abilities (e.g., `canDelete = (deleteSupported && deleteAllowed) || (grafanaDeleteSupported && grafanaDeleteAllowed)`). At the same time, the Grafana list path was refactored to stop fetching ruler-rule data (GrafanaGroupLoader now renders only `promResponse.data.groups...rules` and GrafanaRuleListItem calls `RuleActionsButtons` with only `promRule`). This creates a concrete refactor risk: menu items may become enabled purely from `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` even when no `rulerRule` is present. The finding’s specific claim that the click handlers *still require* a ruler rule (and therefore will definitely fail) is not directly verifiable from the provided diff because the menu-item handler implementations in AlertRuleMenu aren’t shown here, but the concern is diff-grounded and nontrivial.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx:41 dropped the paused-state fallback — old code used rule?.isPaused ?? is_paused, new code uses only rule?.isPaused, so if the Prometheus API omits/nulls isPaused, paused rules render as unpaused

adjudication.rationale: While the old, deleted GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx did set `isPaused: rule?.isPaused ?? is_paused` (falling back to the Ruler rule’s `is_paused`), the new GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx only renders from a required `GrafanaPromRuleDTO` (`rule` prop is non-optional) and sets `isPaused: rule?.isPaused`. In the diff, `GrafanaPromRuleDTOBase` defines `isPaused: boolean` (required), so there’s no diff-grounded evidence that `isPaused` can be omitted/null from the Prometheus API response. Also, this refactor removes rendering of “ruler-only” items entirely (GrafanaGroupLoader now maps only Prometheus rules), so the prior fallback use-case no longer applies.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: useAbilities.ts useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable returns { isEditable: false, isRemovable: false, loading: false } when !rule || !folderUID, treating 'no data yet' as definitively not editable; combined with MaybeSupported = loading ? NotSupported : AlwaysSupported this yields 'supported but denied' during load, causing UI flicker between actions hidden and visible, and invalid/missing folderUid silently removes all actions with no surfaced error

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable` returns `{ isEditable: false, isRemovable: false, loading: false }` when `!rule || !folderUID`, and that `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` sets `MaybeSupported = loading ? NotSupported : AlwaysSupported`. This can yield a transient state where actions are hidden while `useFolder()` is still loading (because `loading` is true and `MaybeSupported` becomes `NotSupported`), then become visible once folder metadata arrives, i.e. potential UI flicker. However, the finding’s specific claim that this combination yields “supported but denied during load” is not strictly accurate for the folder-loading case (during loading it is marked unsupported, not supported). Also, missing `folderUid` is not clearly a new real-world defect in this diff because `GrafanaPromRuleDTOBase.folderUid` is typed as required; the behavior is more of an edge-case/UX/error-handling concern than a verifiable functional break.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx getEditableIdentifier calls logWarning('Unable to construct an editable rule identifier') during render on every render in the fallback path, spamming the analytics/warning channel at poll frequency for consumers passing only a non-Grafana prom rule

adjudication.rationale: In RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx, getEditableIdentifier() calls logWarning('Unable to construct an editable rule identifier') in the fallback path, and this function is invoked during component render (const identifier = getEditableIdentifier(...);). If a caller provides only promRule where prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(promRule) is false (and no ruler `rule`), the warning will fire on every render before returning null. This is a real, diff-grounded concern (side effects/log spam during render), though it doesn’t directly break correctness.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx:31 dropped the returnTo parameter from rule view links — old code appended { returnTo } via createReturnTo(), so users navigating to a rule lose the return-to-list-with-filters-preserved behavior

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a concrete regression: the deleted GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx previously built rule view links as `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo })` using `createReturnTo()`, while the new GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx now sets `href: createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`)` with no `returnTo` parameter. Since FilterView now renders GrafanaRuleListItem directly, users coming from the filtered list would no longer get the prior return-to-list behavior preserved via `returnTo`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Tests: RulesTable.test.tsx / GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx mocks hard-code the hook contract, so plural-hook tests pass even if per-action semantics change, and the deleted matchRules unit tests removed coverage for the ruler/prom propagation-race behavior

adjudication.rationale: In RulesTable.test.tsx the new plural-hook mocks are implemented as `actions.map(...)` (e.g. `mocks.useRulerRuleAbilities.mockImplementation((_rule, _groupIdentifier, actions) => actions.map(() => [false,false]))` and similar per-test overrides), which bakes in the current hook contract (order/1:1 mapping to the input actions) and can allow tests to keep passing even if the hook’s per-action semantics/return shape changes. Also, GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx removes and no longer exports `matchRules`, and GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx deletes the entire `describe('matchRules', ...)` block; this undeniably drops unit coverage for the prior ruler/prom mismatch/propagation-race handling (`promOnlyRules`, “creating/deleting” states), even if that behavior is intentionally removed by the refactor.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Permission checks weakened by OR-ing two independent ability sources: canX = (rulerSupported && rulerAllowed) || (grafanaSupported && grafanaAllowed) allows users denied on one surface but with incidental ability on the other to see and initiate actions (privilege inflation / client-side authz bypass)

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly broadens action gating by OR-ing abilities from two different sources. In `AlertRuleMenu.tsx`, each `canX` is computed as `(pauseSupported && pauseAllowed) || (grafanaPauseSupported && grafanaPauseAllowed)` (same pattern for Delete/Duplicate/Silence/Export). In `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx`, `canEditRule` is similarly OR-ed between `useRulerRuleAbility` and `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility`. This means if one ability source denies an action but the other returns allowed, the UI will still enable/offer the action, which is a verifiable weakening of client-side authorization logic introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stale ruler-based ability path still consulted for Grafana rules: useRulerRuleAbilities treats undefined rule with defaults and derives rulesSourceName from groupIdentifier alone, allowing provisioned/plugin-provided rules to appear actionable and bypassing immutability guards

adjudication.rationale: The diff does make `useRulerRuleAbilities` accept `RulerRuleDTO | undefined` and `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` derives `rulesSourceName` from `groupIdentifier`, but an `undefined` rule does not cause actions to become allowed: `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` sets `isProvisioned` to `false` only when `rule` is missing, yet support/allow still depends on `useIsRuleEditable(rulesSourceName, rule)` and `isRulerAvailable`/`isEditable`/`isRemovable` (which cannot become permissive without a real rule/folder context). For Grafana list-view cases, the menu/buttons now OR ruler-based abilities with the new prom-based abilities (`useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` / `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility`) and the Grafana-prom path explicitly enforces immutability via `isProvisionedPromRule(rule)` and `isPluginProvidedRule(rule)` plus `MaybeSupportedUnlessImmutable`. So the claim that the stale ruler path lets provisioned/plugin-provided rules appear actionable or bypass immutability guards is not supported by the shown code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities marks all actions AlwaysSupported once loading completes, removing the 'feature unavailable' guard and making the grafana path's supported half always true so the effective gate is purely grafanaAllowed

adjudication.rationale: In `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, the “supported” half is not made universally true after loading. While `MaybeSupported` becomes `AlwaysSupported` when `loading` is false, many actions still gate support on rule type and immutability, e.g. `Pause/Restore/DeletePermanently` use `MaybeSupportedUnlessImmutable && isAlertingRule`, `Duplicate` is `NotSupported` for plugin-provided rules, and `Silence` support comes from `useGrafanaRulesSilenceSupport()`. The finding’s claim that the supported half becomes always true so gating is purely “allowed” misreads the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: N+1 folder/permission queries per rule row: useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities/useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable call useFolder(rule?.folderUid) and useCanSilenceInFolder per rule component, causing per-row fan-out of folder lookups, hook executions, and re-render work across ~80 rules per list page

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces per-rule ability evaluation for Grafana Prom rules that performs folder-based permission checks inside the ability hook. Specifically, `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(rule)` calls `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable(rule)` which calls `useFolder(rule?.folderUid)` (new in `useAbilities.ts`), and also calls `useCanSilenceInFolder(rule?.folderUid)`. These are then used via `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility`/`useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, which are invoked from per-row UI components (e.g., `RuleActionsButtons.V2` now calls `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility(..., AlertRuleAction.Update)` and `AlertRuleMenu` calls `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(...)`). In the new list rendering path (`GrafanaGroupLoader` -> `GrafanaRuleListItem` -> `RuleActionsButtons`), this means each rule row can trigger its own folder lookup and related hook work, plausibly creating N-per-row fan-out and extra re-renders across large lists. This is a performance/architecture concern visible in the diff, not a functional correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicate ability computation in AlertRuleMenu: both useRulerRuleAbilities and useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities always execute (10 ability evaluations per menu render), including useIsRuleEditable and useCanSilence(undefined) when rulerRule is undefined, doubling hook execution cost

adjudication.rationale: In AlertRuleMenu.tsx, both `useRulerRuleAbilities(rulerRule, ...)` and `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(..., ...)` are invoked unconditionally on every render, and each is requested with 5 actions, yielding 10 ability lookups total. The diff also shows `useRulerRuleAbilities` now accepts `RulerRuleDTO | undefined` and still calls `useAllRulerRuleAbilities(rule, groupIdentifier)`, which in turn calls `useIsRuleEditable(rulesSourceName, rule)` and `useCanSilence(rule)` even when `rule` is undefined. This is a concrete perf/duplication concern introduced by the change, not a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unstable actions array defeats memoization: AlertRuleMenu passes a new inline actions array literal each render, causing useMemo(() => actions.map(...)) in useRulerRuleAbilities/useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities to recompute every render and change returned Ability[] identity, breaking downstream memo/consumer equality

adjudication.rationale: In AlertRuleMenu.tsx the calls to useRulerRuleAbilities(..., [AlertRuleAction.Pause, ...]) and useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(..., [AlertRuleAction.Pause, ...]) pass fresh inline array literals each render. In useAbilities.ts both hooks memoize with useMemo(..., [abilities, actions]); because `actions` is a new array identity each render, the memoization will always recompute and return a new Ability[] identity. This is a performance/identity-stability issue grounded in the diff, but it does not constitute a functional correctness defect by itself (the computed abilities remain correct).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Ability checks OR'd together grant actions when only one path allows them, potentially allowing federated/provisioned rules to appear editable/deletable in the UI (privilege escalation risk in UI)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce OR’d ability checks (e.g., `canEditRule = (editSupported && editAllowed) || (grafanaEditSupported && grafanaEditAllowed)` in `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx`, and similar `canPause/canDelete/...` ORs in `AlertRuleMenu.tsx`). While the OR itself doesn’t clearly bypass provisioned-rule gating (Grafana Prom path now checks `provenance` via `isProvisionedPromRule`, and both paths require `supported && allowed`), the diff *does* remove federated immutability handling: in `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` it hard-codes `const isFederated = false; // TODO`, whereas the previous `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` used `isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` to make such rules immutable. That regression can cause federated rules to appear editable/deletable in the UI, which matches the core risk described (even if the OR is not the direct cause).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Grafana prom-rule path does not check isProvisioned for silence, and previous federated-rule immutability enforcement has silently been dropped

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly removes federated-rule immutability enforcement for ruler-backed rules: in `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` it now hardcodes `const isFederated = false;` with a TODO, whereas previously `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` computed `isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` and included it in `immutableRule` (blocking edit/delete/etc). This is a concrete behavior change that can incorrectly allow modifications of federated rules. The other claim about silence needing an `isProvisioned` check on the Grafana Prom-rule path is not clearly implied/required by the diff (silence is now gated by `silenceSupported` and folder permission + `isAlertingRule`), but the federated immutability drop is verifiable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities asserts support before permissions load; if rule is defined but folderUid is missing, useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable permanently reports non-editable/non-removable with loading:false, so edit/delete buttons never appear

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable`, which returns `{isEditable:false,isRemovable:false,loading:false}` when `!rule || !folderUID` (so if `folderUid` were missing/empty at runtime, edit/delete would indeed never become allowed). However, within this diff `GrafanaPromRuleDTOBase` defines `folderUid: string` (required) and all new call sites pass Prometheus-provided `GrafanaPromRuleDTO` objects, so the finding’s premise (“rule is defined but folderUid is missing”) is not evidenced by the diff. Also, `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` does not “assert support before permissions load”; it explicitly sets `MaybeSupported = loading ? NotSupported : AlwaysSupported`, i.e., hides support while folder perms load.

adjudication_records.issue_text: useGrafanaPromRuleAbility/useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities fetch folder permissions unconditionally per rule, causing N+1 folder metadata HTTP requests on the alert list page even for rules that end up skipped

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities()`, which calls `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable()`, and that in turn calls `useFolder(folderUID)` on every hook invocation (even when `rule` is `undefined`, since it still executes `useFolder(rule?.folderUid)`). The new `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility/Abilities` are used in list-item UI (`RuleActionsButtons.V2` and `AlertRuleMenu`), so for each rendered rule this can trigger per-rule folder lookups (and even for `skipToken` paths the hook still runs). Whether this becomes actual N+1 HTTP requests depends on `useFolder` caching/behavior (not shown in the diff), so it’s a grounded performance/architecture concern rather than a proven functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Deleting/creating state indicators removed entirely from the Grafana list view: RuleOperation.Creating and RuleOperation.Deleting transitional states no longer rendered, so users lose feedback during ruler/prometheus propagation lag

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the logic that rendered transitional RuleOperation states in the Grafana list view. In GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx, the ruler query (useGetGrafanaRulerGroupQuery), matchRules(), and the conditional rendering of RuleOperation.Creating (for ruler-only rules) and RuleOperationListItem with RuleOperation.Deleting (for prom-only rules) are deleted, and the component now renders only promResponse.data.groups.at(0)?.rules without passing any operation prop. While this does eliminate the creating/deleting indicators, the diff also suggests an intentional shift away from ruler API calls/propagation handling, so it's not verifiably a correctness defect from the diff alone—more a UX/behavior change risk if propagation lag still exists.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RulesTable.test.tsx 'Grafana rules: should not render Edit button' test mocks useGrafanaPromRuleAbility (singular) which AlertRuleMenu never calls, making the mock dead code and the test not faithfully pinning the component-to-hook contract

adjudication.rationale: In `RulesTable.test.tsx`, the `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility` (singular) mock is not dead code for the “should not render Edit button” test because `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx` directly calls `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility(..., AlertRuleAction.Update)` to decide whether to render the Edit button. While it’s true `AlertRuleMenu.tsx` uses the plural `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` hook (and not the singular one), that’s unrelated to the Edit button assertion, and the test also mocks `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` for the menu path anyway.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Plural useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities default mock ignores the rule argument, so a non-Grafana promRule would still return [true,true], masking a real bug if the prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule() guard were removed

adjudication.rationale: In `RulesTable.test.tsx`, the default plural hook mocks (`useRulerRuleAbilities`, `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`) are implemented as `actions.map(() => [false, false])`, and several test-specific overrides also map only on `action`—they never assert/branch on the `rule` argument. That means the tests would still pass even if `AlertRuleMenu` stopped using the `prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(promRule) ? promRule : skipToken` guard and incorrectly called the hook with a non-Grafana `promRule`, because the mocked hook behavior does not depend on the passed rule. However, the finding’s specific claim that the *default* mock would return `[true,true]` for non-Grafana rules is not accurate (the default is `[false,false]`). The underlying point is a test robustness gap, not an app defect shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AlertRuleMenu silence support comes from two divergent sources (useCanSilence vs prom hook abilities) OR'd together, so type-detection mismatch between RulerGrafanaRuleDTO and GrafanaPromRuleDTO can show Silence menu items for invalid rules or hide previously working ones

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce two different silence-ability sources that are OR’d together in AlertRuleMenu: ruler-based abilities via `useRulerRuleAbilities(...)/useAllRulerRuleAbilities` (which sets `[AlertRuleAction.Silence]` from `useCanSilence(rule)`) and prom-based abilities via `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(...)/useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` (which sets Silence as `[silenceSupported, canSilenceInFolder && isAlertingRule]`). This divergence is real and could lead to inconsistent UI behavior if the two sources disagree. However, the specific claim that a type-detection mismatch between `RulerGrafanaRuleDTO` and `GrafanaPromRuleDTO` will definitively show Silence for invalid rules or hide valid ones is not directly verifiable from the diff alone (we can’t see `useCanSilence`’s internal logic, and prom abilities are gated by `prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(promRule) ? promRule : skipToken`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: useRulerRuleAbilities signature widened to accept undefined but the body may not guard against undefined, risking a runtime crash for callers passing undefined

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `useRulerRuleAbilities` now accepts `rule: RulerRuleDTO | undefined`, but its implementation (as shown) does not dereference `rule` at all; it just calls `useAllRulerRuleAbilities(rule, groupIdentifier)` and maps returned `abilities`. Additionally, `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` in this diff explicitly guards `rule` being undefined (e.g., `const isProvisioned = rule ? isProvisionedRule(rule) : false;` and passes `rule` directly to `useIsRuleEditable`). The claimed “body may not guard against undefined” for `useRulerRuleAbilities` is not supported by what’s visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: OR-combining abilities bypasses 'supported' gating — combining (rulerSupported && rulerAllowed) || (grafanaSupported && grafanaAllowed) can expose edit/delete/pause buttons when the ruler API is unavailable but user has folder permissions, causing operations to fail at execution time; ability checks should require both paths to agree on support

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce OR-combined ability gating in multiple places (e.g., AlertRuleMenu.tsx: `canPause/canDelete/... = (rulerSupported && rulerAllowed) || (grafanaSupported && grafanaAllowed)` and RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx similarly for Update), and the new `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` treats GrafanaPromRuleDTO actions as broadly supported (`MaybeSupported = loading ? NotSupported : AlwaysSupported`) without any “ruler availability” concept. However, the claim that this will "cause operations to fail at execution time" when the ruler API is unavailable is not verifiable from this diff because the execution paths for pause/delete/edit aren’t shown here. What is verifiable is a potentially inconsistent support model across backends due to the OR logic and the AlwaysSupported assumption, which is a concrete, diff-grounded design/edge-case concern but not a proven defect from the provided changes alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Provisioning/immutability detection inconsistency — ruler path uses rule.grafana_alert.provenance while prom path uses isProvisionedPromRule/Boolean(provenance) from the prom DTO; if the APIs disagree on provenance, provisioned rules can be marked mutable and expose destructive Delete/Edit actions (data-loss vector)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces two separate immutability/provisioning signals: Ruler path uses `isProvisionedRule(rule)` (checks `rule.grafana_alert.provenance`), while the new Prom path uses `isProvisionedPromRule(promRule)` (checks `promRule.provenance`, newly added as optional). Components like `AlertRuleMenu` and `RuleActionsButtons.V2` then OR the results from ruler-abilities and prom-abilities (e.g., `canDelete = (rulerSupported&&rulerAllowed) || (grafanaSupported&&grafanaAllowed)`), meaning if the two APIs ever disagree on provenance/immutability, the more permissive result wins and could surface Edit/Delete actions. The diff does not prove the APIs can disagree, so this is a risk/consistency concern rather than a verifiable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Refactor drops 'Creating'/'Deleting' rule state rendering and ruler-API reconciliation in GrafanaGroupLoader — ruler-only and prom-only transition rules no longer show indicators and the logWarning telemetry for mismatched rules was removed, making stuck/failing rule propagation invisible in the UI

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes ruler-API reconciliation and the transitional UI states in GrafanaGroupLoader. Specifically, GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx no longer calls useGetGrafanaRulerGroupQuery, deletes matchRules(), and stops rendering ruler-only rules as "Creating" and prom-only rules as "Deleting" (RuleOperationListItem block removed). The prior logWarning telemetry for mismatched prom-only rules is also deleted along with matchRules(). This is a real, diff-grounded loss of observability/UX for propagation inconsistencies, but the diff alone doesn’t prove it is a correctness defect (it could be an intentional assumption of strong consistency).

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable/useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities conflate 'folder missing' with 'loading' — folder query errors leave MaybeSupported as AlwaysSupported so actions like Silence/Duplicate/Export still appear; no error-state handling for the folder query and rule-level check no longer factors isRulerAvailable into support

adjudication.rationale: In useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(), support is computed as `MaybeSupported = loading ? NotSupported : AlwaysSupported`. But useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable() only returns `{ folder, loading }` from useFolder() and has no error state; when `folder` is missing and `loading` is false (e.g., folder query error or invalid UID), it returns `{ isEditable:false, isRemovable:false, loading:false }`, which makes `MaybeSupported` become AlwaysSupported. That means abilities whose *allowed* side is purely global (e.g., Duplicate uses `rulesPermissions.create`, Export uses `exportAllowed`) can end up with `supported=true` even though folder resolution failed. Also, passing `skipToken` maps to `rule === undefined`, and for `rule` undefined the hook still yields `Duplicate` as supported (since `loading` is false), so `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(...skipToken...)` can incorrectly contribute to `canDuplicate` in AlertRuleMenu via the OR logic. This is a concrete behavior issue introduced by the new hooks’ loading/missing-folder handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: returnTo dropped from rule list item links in GrafanaRuleListItem — new href omits returnTo from createReturnTo(), breaking back-navigation to the list view after viewing a rule

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the `returnTo` parameter from Grafana rule list item links. Previously, `GrafanaRuleLoader`’s `GrafanaRuleListItem` computed `const returnTo = createReturnTo();` and built `href: createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo })`. The new `public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx` now sets `href: createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`)` with no `returnTo`. This is a concrete behavior change in the generated link and can reasonably break “back to list” navigation that relies on `returnTo`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: useAllAlertRuleAbilities changed rulesSourceName derivation from getRulesSourceName(rule.namespace.rulesSource) to groupIdentifier origin — for federated/copied groups the permissions may be evaluated against the wrong data source

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` to derive the rules source via `groupIdentifier.fromCombinedRule(rule)` and then `getGroupOriginName(groupIdentifier)` (in `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`) instead of the prior `getRulesSourceName(rule.namespace.rulesSource)`. That is a real, diff-grounded behavior change and could affect which permissions bucket (`getRulesPermissions(rulesSourceName)`) is used if `groupIdentifier` origin can differ from `rule.namespace.rulesSource`. However, the diff does not demonstrate federated/copied group cases or prove that `groupIdentifier` would be wrong for them, so the claim of a definite bug is not verifiable from the PR alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Unused variable/redundant guard in GrafanaRuleListItem — promAlertingRule guard is redundant since rule is non-optional; flag to confirm prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule narrows the type correctly

adjudication.rationale: In `GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx`, `promAlertingRule` is not unused—it is used to compute `instancesCount` and to pass `state` to `AlertRuleListItem`. While `rule &&` inside `const promAlertingRule = rule && rule.type === PromRuleType.Alerting ? rule : undefined;` is redundant because `rule` is a required prop, that’s a minor style/nit and not the “unused variable” claimed. Also, whether `prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` performs TypeScript narrowing cannot be verified from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RulesTable tests mock useRulerRuleAbilities and useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities, so the real hook implementations and the OR-combining logic in AlertRuleMenu.tsx and RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx are completely untested; a bug in the OR logic or skipToken guard would pass the suite

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `RulesTable.test.tsx` mocks `../../hooks/useAbilities` and provides mocked implementations for both plural hooks used by `AlertRuleMenu` (`useRulerRuleAbilities`, `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`) and the singular prom hook (`useGrafanaPromRuleAbility`). That means the real implementations added/changed in `useAbilities.ts` (including the `skipToken` handling in `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility/useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` and the new ability computation in `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`) are not exercised by these tests. While the OR-combining logic in `AlertRuleMenu.tsx` / `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx` still runs with mocked return values, a regression in the real `skipToken` guard or real ability computation could indeed pass this suite because the hooks are fully mocked here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The OR-combination logic (canX = (rulerSupported && rulerAllowed) || (grafanaSupported && grafanaAllowed)) has zero behavioral tests, missing cases like ruler-supported-only, supported-but-not-allowed, undefined promRule with non-grafana ruler rule, and non-alerting grafana prom rules (e.g., recording rules should not show Pause)

adjudication.rationale: This diff introduces new OR-combination permission logic in `AlertRuleMenu` (e.g., `const canPause = (pauseSupported && pauseAllowed) || (grafanaPauseSupported && grafanaPauseAllowed);` and similarly for Delete/Duplicate/Silence/Export) by combining results from `useRulerRuleAbilities(...)` and `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(..., skipToken)`. While several tests were updated/added, they mainly assert button/menu presence under a single mocked source of truth (e.g., RulesTable mocks often drive only the Grafana-prom side or only the ruler side) and do not explicitly cover the mixed/edge scenarios implied by the new OR logic (e.g., supported-but-not-allowed on one side, ruler-only vs grafana-only, promRule skipped via `skipToken`, or grafana recording rule vs alerting rule behavior for Pause/Silence). That makes the finding a concrete, diff-grounded gap in behavioral coverage for newly added nontrivial logic rather than a proven functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GrafanaGroupLoader behavioral change removes Creating/Deleting states with old tests deleted, not replaced; no test covers a rule existing in prom whose ruler rule was just deleted, risking rules silently disappearing with no indicator or logWarning

adjudication.rationale: Diff shows GrafanaGroupLoader no longer queries the Ruler API or runs `matchRules`; it now renders only `promResponse.data.groups.at(0)?.rules` and removes the `RuleOperationListItem` “Deleting” path and the `logWarning` from `matchRules` (which is deleted). Corresponding tests for “only ruler rule exists (Creating)” and “only prom rule exists (Deleting)” plus all `matchRules` tests were removed and replaced with menu/action tests, leaving no coverage for those transitional/consistency edge cases. However, the finding’s claim that a prom-only rule would “silently disappear” is not supported by the new code (prom-only rules would still render, just without a deleting indicator).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Deleted matchRules unit tests leave no coverage for the new single-source rendering edge cases: a group with zero rules and a response where groups is empty (at(0) undefined) silently rendering an empty list

adjudication.rationale: In GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx the render path uses `promResponse.data.groups.at(0)?.rules.map(...)`. If `groups` is empty, `at(0)` is `undefined`, so `at(0)?.rules` evaluates to `undefined` and then `.map(...)` is invoked on `undefined`, causing a runtime crash (not a safe empty render). The diff also removed the prior matching logic/tests, and no new test covers the `groups: []` case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New hooks useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities / useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable lack direct tests for edge cases: missing folderUid, folder still loading (should suppress buttons, not flash-deny), undefined rule/skipToken path, provisioned rules with provenance, and non-alerting rules

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new nontrivial logic paths in `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities()` and its helper `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable()` (e.g., `if (!rule || !folderUID) return { isEditable: false, isRemovable: false, loading: false }`, `if (!folder) return { ..., loading }`, and the `skipToken`-based APIs `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility/Abilities`). Existing/updated tests (e.g., `GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx`, `RulesTable.test.tsx`) exercise some RBAC/menu rendering, but they do not directly cover the edge cases called out: missing `folderUid`, folder still loading, `skipToken`/undefined rule behavior, provisioned rules via new `provenance` field (`isProvisionedPromRule`), or non-alerting Grafana prom rules affecting silence/export/pause gating (`isAlertingRule`). This is a specific, diff-grounded test coverage gap rather than a demonstrated functional defect in the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GrafanaGroupLoader test hard-codes 'exactly 4 menu items' while granting Delete permission but never asserting Delete is present (implicitly asserting its absence); the brittle count also breaks if legitimate menu items are added

adjudication.rationale: In `GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx`, the `beforeEach` grants delete-related permissions (`AccessControlAction.AlertingRuleDelete`) via both `grantUserPermissions([...AlertingRuleDelete...])` and `setFolderAccessControl({ [AlertingRuleDelete]: true, ... })`. However, the test `should render correct menu actions when More button is clicked` asserts only `silence`, `copyLink`, `duplicate`, and `export`, and then hard-codes `expect(menuItems.length).toBe(4)`, never asserting the `delete` menu item (even though a selector `menuItems.delete` is defined). This makes the test brittle (will break if a legitimate item is added) and potentially inconsistent with the granted permissions/expected UI behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RulesTable cloud-rule tests assert only the mock (skipToken) rather than verified behavior; nothing verifies that a real Mimir/cloud rule correctly passes skipToken to useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities via the prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule type-guard

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces conditional use of `skipToken` when calling `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` (e.g., in `AlertRuleMenu`: `prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(promRule) ? promRule : skipToken`). In `RulesTable.test.tsx`, the cloud-rule cases explicitly rely on the assumption that `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` receives `skipToken` (“gets skipToken”) and therefore only mock `useRulerRuleAbilities`, but they do not assert the type-guard behavior or the actual argument passed to `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`. This is a concrete test coverage gap for newly added branching logic, not a demonstrated runtime defect in the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: useAbilities.ts hardcodes isFederated = false with a TODO, dropping federated-rule immutability handling and showing Edit/Delete/Pause to users whose edits won't behave correctly (behavioral regression)

adjudication.rationale: In `useAbilities.ts`, `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` previously computed federation via `isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` (see removed code) and used it in `immutableRule = isProvisioned || isFederated || isPluginProvided` to disable edit/delete/pause for federated rules. The diff replaces this with `// TODO: Add support for federated rules` and hardcodes `const isFederated = false;`, which will incorrectly treat federated rules as mutable and can expose actions (Update/Delete/Pause/Restore, etc.) that should be unsupported/blocked for federated rule groups. That is a behavioral regression introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GrafanaGroupLoader no longer handles ruler/prom divergence: removed useGetGrafanaRulerGroupQuery, matchRules, and Creating/Deleting rendering, so rules silently vanish from the list during propagation and the logWarning mismatch observability is lost

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the divergence-handling path in `GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx`: `useGetGrafanaRulerGroupQuery` is removed, `matchRules` is deleted (along with its `logWarning`), and the rendering of `RuleOperationListItem` for `Creating`/`Deleting` states is dropped. The loader now renders only `promResponse.data.groups.at(0)?.rules` and shows an error only when `promResponse` is missing. This is a real, diff-grounded loss of robustness/observability for the case where Ruler and Prometheus are temporarily inconsistent, but the diff itself doesn’t prove such divergence still occurs (the removed code even comments that Grafana Prom rules “should be strongly consistent now”), so it’s better classified as an edge-case/scope concern rather than a verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: hooks/useAbilities.ts duplicates ability-checking logic: useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable re-implements useIsRuleEditable (marked '// duplicate') and useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities copies ~60 lines of useAllRulerRuleAbilities, creating two parallel permission engines with drift risk

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly introduces a parallel ability/permission path for Grafana Prom rules: `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities()` largely mirrors the structure of `useAllRulerRuleAbilities()` (provisioned/plugin/immutable checks, permissions mapping, action->ability table), and it adds a new `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable()` with an inline comment `// duplicate`, which re-implements edit/remove checks using folder ACLs instead of reusing `useIsRuleEditable`. This is not a direct functional defect by itself, but it is a concrete, diff-grounded maintainability/architecture concern because it creates two separate “permission engines” that can drift (e.g., differences in supported actions, immutable-rule rules, loading semantics).

adjudication_records.issue_text: AlertRuleMenu.tsx has five copy-pasted 'OR two ability tuples' blocks (canPause, canDelete, canDuplicate, canSilence, canExport) with questionable OR semantics where the permissive path wins; should be centralized in a combineAbilities helper

adjudication.rationale: In AlertRuleMenu.tsx the diff introduces five nearly identical blocks that destructure a ruler ability tuple and a Grafana-prom ability tuple and then compute `canX = (supported && allowed) || (grafanaSupported && grafanaAllowed)` for Pause/Delete/Duplicate/Silence/ModifyExport. This duplication is verifiable and a `combineAbilities` helper would reduce repetition and the chance of inconsistent future changes. However, the claim that the OR semantics are definitively wrong is not provable from the diff alone (the added comments suggest the intent is to allow the action if either ability source grants it).

adjudication_records.issue_text: useAllAlertRuleAbilities derives rules source from group origin instead of the rule's namespace rulesSource, potentially querying editability against the wrong datasource for mismatched combined rules

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` no longer derives the rules source from `rule.namespace.rulesSource` (old code), and instead constructs a `groupIdentifier` via `groupIdentifier.fromCombinedRule(rule)` and then `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` derives `rulesSourceName` from `getGroupOriginName(groupIdentifier)`. That is a real behavioral change in how the rules source is determined for editability/permissions (`useIsRuleEditable(rulesSourceName, rule)`), and the finding’s concern about potential mismatch is plausible. However, the diff does not show whether `groupIdentifier.fromCombinedRule` can diverge from `rule.namespace.rulesSource`, so an actual wrong-datasource query cannot be verified from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Custom skipToken Symbol in useAbilities.ts collides conceptually with RTK Query's skipToken sentinel, causing import and reader confusion; should be renamed (e.g. skipAbility) or reuse RTK concept

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `export const skipToken = Symbol('ability-skip-token');` in `useAbilities.ts` and then imports `skipToken` in UI components (e.g., `AlertRuleMenu.tsx`, `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx`). RTK Query commonly exports a sentinel also named `skipToken`, so having a different, locally-defined `skipToken` in the same codebase can plausibly create reader/import ambiguity and future naming conflicts (especially in files that might also use RTK Query). This is a maintainability/clarity issue rather than a verifiable runtime bug from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GrafanaRuleListItem drops is_paused fallback, provenance, and returnTo navigation context sourced from the ruler rule, so paused/provisioned indicators and back-navigation silently disappear if the Prometheus API doesn't return them

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows GrafanaRuleListItem is refactored to use only the Prometheus API rule (GrafanaPromRuleDTO) and no longer receives the ruler rule. In the new GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx, `href` is built as `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`)` with no `returnTo` context, whereas the deleted GrafanaRuleLoader/GrafanaRuleListItem used `createRelativeUrl(..., { returnTo })`. Also, paused/provisioned flags now come only from the Prom rule (`isPaused: rule?.isPaused`, `isProvisioned: Boolean(provenance)`) and the previous fallback to `rulerRule.grafana_alert.is_paused` / `rulerRule.grafana_alert.provenance` is gone. Whether Prometheus will always return equivalent fields is not verifiable from the diff (provenance was added to the DTO, suggesting intent to provide it), so the finding is a grounded edge-case/UX regression concern rather than a confirmed defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RulesTable.test.tsx duplicates mock implementations of up to 3-4 ability hooks per test and in beforeEach; should use a shared mockAbilities helper

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show repeated per-test mocking in `RulesTable.test.tsx` (e.g., multiple tests re-`mockImplementation` for `useAlertRuleAbility`, `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, and `useRulerRuleAbilities`, plus default mocks in `beforeEach`). However, the finding is essentially a maintainability/style refactor suggestion (introduce a shared helper) rather than a specific correctness/behavior issue created by the PR, so it doesn’t meet the bar for an “important_non_bug” under the provided rules.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RuleActionsButtons.V2 props type uses RequireAtLeastOne over two optional fields, which doesn't actually enforce at least one, and getEditableIdentifier/getIsProvisioned handle undefined/undefined at runtime; type should be a union like { rule } | { promRule }

adjudication.rationale: In RuleActionsButtons.V2 the props are typed as `RequireAtLeastOne<{ rule?: RulerRuleDTO; promRule?: Rule; }>` which (per type-fest’s contract) does enforce that at least one of the keys is present; it does not allow `rule` and `promRule` to both be omitted in well-typed call sites. The added runtime guards in `getIsProvisioned` / `getEditableIdentifier` handle the impossible-in-types case defensively, but the finding’s claim that the type “doesn’t actually enforce at least one” is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: useRulerRuleAbilities now accepts RulerRuleDTO | undefined and silently returns all-NotSupported abilities instead of a type error, moving the 'which rule am I checking' guard concern from types to call sites

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes `useRulerRuleAbilities` to accept `rule: RulerRuleDTO | undefined` (in `useAbilities.ts`). Downstream, `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` is also written to tolerate `undefined` and compute abilities that effectively become unsupported when `rule` is missing (e.g., `const isProvisioned = rule ? isProvisionedRule(rule) : false;` and `MaybeSupported` depends on `isRulerAvailable`, which will be falsey when no rule info is available). This removes the previous type-level guarantee that callers must supply a `RulerRuleDTO`, shifting “which rule am I checking?” to runtime/call-site logic. That’s a legitimate design/architecture concern grounded in the diff, but not a directly verifiable functional defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: OR-union of ruler and grafana ability checks in AlertRuleMenu.tsx and RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx can grant actions the backend will reject, since the button can appear when only the other permission path said yes

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce OR-union permission gating in both AlertRuleMenu.tsx (e.g., `canDelete = (deleteSupported && deleteAllowed) || (grafanaDeleteSupported && grafanaDeleteAllowed)`) and RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx (`canEditRule` uses the same OR pattern). That is a concrete change: UI actions can become visible if either the Ruler-based or GrafanaProm-based ability path returns allowed. However, the finding’s stronger claim that this will "grant actions the backend will reject" is not verifiable from the diff alone because the diff does not show which backend endpoints are invoked for each action nor how those endpoints authorize requests. So the issue is a real, diff-grounded design/consistency concern (potential for mismatched authorization models), but the backend-rejection behavior is speculative from the provided changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: OR-union of ability checks masks permission bugs — if either hook is wrong, the other path's correct 'no' is silently overridden with no reconciliation or logging when the two disagree

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly combines permissions via OR across two independent ability sources with no reconciliation/logging: e.g. in `AlertRuleMenu.tsx` `canPause/canDelete/...` are computed as `(rulerSupported && rulerAllowed) || (grafanaSupported && grafanaAllowed)`, and in `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx` `canEditRule` is computed the same way using `useRulerRuleAbility` and `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility`. This does mean a disagreement between the two sources is silently resolved to “allowed” if either path returns allowed, which can hide bugs/inconsistencies between the hooks. However, the diff alone doesn’t prove an actual incorrect permission grant occurs; it just introduces an architecture/diagnostic risk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx rewrite removes ruler API fetch, so ruler-only rules (in 'Creating' state) vanish from the list until the prom rules endpoint catches up

adjudication.rationale: The rewrite of GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx removes the ruler API fetch (useGetGrafanaRulerGroupQuery) and the logic that rendered ruler-only rules as `RuleOperation.Creating` when no matching Prom rule existed. Previously, the component iterated `rulerResponse?.rules` and, when `matches.get(rulerRule)` was missing, still rendered a `GrafanaRuleListItem` with `operation={RuleOperation.Creating}`. Now it only renders `promResponse.data.groups.at(0)?.rules.map((promRule) => <GrafanaRuleListItem ... />)`, so if the Prom endpoint doesn't yet include a newly created rule but it exists in the ruler, it will not appear at all until Prom catches up.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Removal of ruler API fetch means prom-only rules mid-deletion no longer show 'Deleting' state, appearing as live rules with full action buttons including Delete, inviting double-delete confusion

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the Ruler fetch and matching logic that previously detected “prom-only” rules and rendered them as a `RuleOperationListItem` with `operation={RuleOperation.Deleting}` and no action buttons (see deleted block in `GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx` rendering `promOnlyRules.map(...)`). Now `GrafanaGroupLoader` renders *only* `promResponse.data.groups.at(0)?.rules` as normal `GrafanaRuleListItem`s, which attach `actions: <RuleActionsButtons promRule={rule} ... />` (`GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx`). This means any prom-only rule (e.g., mid-deletion propagation) will appear as a live rule with full actions (including Delete if permitted), losing the prior “Deleting” state and enabling double-delete confusion.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Tests in GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx and RulesTable.test.tsx removed the matchRules unit tests and 'Creating'/'Deleting' state assertions, replacing them with happy-path-only tests

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the `matchRules` unit tests and the Creating/Deleting-state assertions from `GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx`, but that coincides with deleting `matchRules` and all Creating/Deleting UI logic from `GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx` (no more ruler API, no `RuleOperationListItem`, no `RuleOperation.Creating/Deleting`). However, the finding incorrectly claims the same removal happened in `RulesTable.test.tsx` (there is no `matchRules` there, and the diff shows RBAC tests being updated/mocked rather than removed). Also, the new `GrafanaGroupLoader` tests are not “happy-path-only” since they include a negative permission case (“should not render edit button when user lacks edit permissions”).

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: RulesTable.test.tsx removed the useRulerRuleAbilities mock while the component ORs both hooks, so the 'should render edit button' test passes if either hook says yes, masking regressions in either hook individually (green-while-red test setup)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not remove the `useRulerRuleAbilities` mock; it is explicitly added to `mocks` and given a default `mockImplementation` in `beforeEach` that returns `[false, false]` for every action. In the “should render Edit button …” tests, `useRulerRuleAbility/useRulerRuleAbilities` remain at their default false values, so the tests only pass if the specifically mocked Grafana/prom abilities return allowed=true (i.e., they are not “green-while-red” via the ruler side). The finding’s premise (“removed the useRulerRuleAbilities mock” and tests passing if either hook says yes) is not supported by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: isPluginProvidedRule is called with a GrafanaPromRuleDTO in useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities where it presumably always returns false, causing plugin-provided Grafana-managed rules to lose their immutability guard and become editable/deletable

adjudication.rationale: In `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` the code sets `const isPluginProvided = isPluginProvidedRule(rule);` where `rule` is a `GrafanaPromRuleDTO | undefined` (new hook intended for Prom-rule DTOs). The immutability guard (`immutableRule = isProvisioned || isFederated || isPluginProvided`) relies on `isPluginProvidedRule` working correctly for this DTO type. The diff does not show `isPluginProvidedRule`’s implementation, so it’s not verifiable that it "always returns false" or that plugin-provided Grafana-managed Prom rules exist; however, the finding is a concrete, diff-grounded risk that the plugin-provided check may no longer apply for GrafanaPromRuleDTOs, potentially weakening the intended immutability logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Type guards rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule) and prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) are invoked with possibly-undefined rule, which may throw at render for consumers passing skipToken/undefined instead of returning 'not supported'

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce new call sites where type-guard helpers are invoked with values that can be `undefined` due to the new `skipToken`/optional rule flow. In `useAbilities.ts`, `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(rule: GrafanaPromRuleDTO | undefined)` calls `prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` even when `rule` is `undefined` (e.g., `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility(..., skipToken, ...)` maps to `undefined`). Similarly, `useAllRulerRuleAbilities(rule: RulerRuleDTO | undefined, ...)` calls `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)` / `isPluginProvidedRule(rule)` with possibly-undefined `rule`. Whether this actually throws depends on the implementations of those helpers (not shown in the diff), so a crash is not verifiable here, but the potential/contract mismatch is a concrete, diff-grounded concern that should be addressed (e.g., guard with `rule && ...` or ensure helpers accept `unknown | undefined`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx drops returnTo from the href, losing 'back to list' navigation context when going from rule list to rule detail

adjudication.rationale: In the deleted GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx, GrafanaRuleListItem built the rule link with `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo })` where `returnTo` came from `createReturnTo()`, preserving “back to list” context. The new GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx sets `href: createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`)` and no longer includes `returnTo`, so the navigation context is lost when clicking from the list to the rule view.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx removed the is_paused fallback (isPaused: rule?.isPaused only), so if the Prometheus rules API omits isPaused for Grafana-managed rules, paused rules will render as unpaused

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the previous fallback `rule?.isPaused ?? is_paused` (old `GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx`) and the new `GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx` uses only `isPaused: rule?.isPaused`. However, the finding’s premise that the Prometheus rules API may omit `isPaused` is not supported by the diff: `GrafanaPromRuleDTOBase` defines `isPaused: boolean` (non-optional), and the new list path no longer has access to `rulerRule.is_paused` anyway. The reported broken behavior depends on an unverified API omission not shown in the PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Provisioned detection switched from ruler rule provenance to prom rule provenance; if the prom endpoint doesn't surface provenance, provisioned rules will appear editable/deletable until UI writes fail

adjudication.rationale: The diff does switch provisioned detection for Grafana list-view paths from Ruler provenance to Prom provenance: `GrafanaRuleListItem` now sets `isProvisioned: Boolean(provenance)` from `GrafanaPromRuleDTO.provenance`, and abilities use `isProvisionedPromRule()` which checks `promRule.provenance` (added as optional in `GrafanaPromRuleDTOBase`). If the Prom endpoint fails to include `provenance`, provisioned rules would be treated as non-provisioned (potentially showing edit/delete). However the diff does not prove whether the Prom API actually omits provenance, so this is a concrete risk/edge-case concern rather than a verifiable defect from the PR alone.
